mainTopic: The ban on dealings before gentile festivals, the spelling of אידיהן/עידיהן and its sources, and the opening of the aggadah about the nations at the end of days
overview: The משנה forbids business and money dealings with גוים for three days before their festivals, because a good deal may lead the גוי to thank his עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה allows collecting a debt from them, since paying hurts the גוי. The חכמים answer that he is relieved afterward. The גמרא reports that רב ושמואל read the משנה's word for 'their festivals' differently: אידיהן with an א (calamity) or עידיהן with an ע (witnesses). Each reading has a פסוק to back it up, and each side explains why its word is better. The גמרא then challenges the פסוק used for the ע reading, since רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it as being about ישראל. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע brings a different פסוק, where the idols themselves are the witnesses. Finally, an aggadah begins about the future: הקב״ה invites those who studied Torah to take their reward, and the nations rush in. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's basic ban before gentile festivals
steps.stepSummary: For three days before a gentile festival, a Jew may not do business, lend or borrow items, lend or borrow money, or repay or collect debts with גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For three days before the festivals of gentiles, it is forbidden to do business with them, to lend items to them or borrow items from them, to lend money to them or borrow money from them, and to repay them or collect payment from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the dealings with גוים that are forbidden during the three days before their festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list comes in pairs, and each pair goes both ways: giving to the גוי and taking from him. A good deal in either direction can make the גוי happy, and the concern is that he will thank his עבודה זרה on his festival.

keyTerms.meaning: To do business (literally, 'to carry and to give')
To lend an item that will be returned as is
To lend money or goods that will be paid back
To collect a debt from them. On its own, לִפְרוֹעַ means to settle a debt, and מֵהֶן ('from them') makes it collecting

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנַי אֵידֵיהֶן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים
phrases.english: Three days before the festivals of gentiles
it is forbidden to do business with them
to lend items to them and to borrow items from them
to lend money to them and to borrow money from them
to repay them and to collect payment from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְנַי אֵידֵיהֶן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the three days before a gentile festival, all business and money dealings with גוים are forbidden, in both directions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the topic for the opening of מסכת עבודה זרה: avoiding anything that would lead a גוי to thank his עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows collecting debts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a Jew may collect a debt from a גוי during these days, because paying makes the גוי sad, not happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One may collect payment from them, because it causes him distress.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with one item on the list. He says collecting a debt from a גוי is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה accepts the reason behind the ban, which is not to make the גוי happy. He argues that paying a debt hurts the גוי, so the reason does not apply to collecting from him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one may collect payment from them
because it causes him distress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the last item of the list in step 1 (collecting from them).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collecting a debt from a גוי is allowed, since it causes him pain and not joy.

steps.title: The Sages answer: he is happy later
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that even though the גוי is sad when he pays, he is happy afterward to be free of the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Even though he is distressed now, he is happy afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the test is whether the גוי ends up happy. The חכמים say we must look at how he feels later, and later he is relieved that the debt is gone. So collecting is also forbidden.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיצֵר הוּא עַכְשָׁיו
phrases.english: even though he is distressed now
he is happy afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's reason for allowing collection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יהודה's claim that collecting a debt brings the גוי no joy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He looked only at the moment of payment and ignored the relief the גוי feels afterward.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה rests on one idea: don't make a גוי happy right before his festival. The disagreement is only about whether paying a debt makes him happy in the end.

steps.title: רב and שמואל read the משנה's word differently
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל disagree about the spelling of the משנה's word for 'their festivals'. One reads אידיהן with an א, and the other reads עידיהן with an ע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב and שמואל: one teaches אידיהן with an א, and one teaches עידיהן with an ע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with an argument about how to read the משנה's word for 'their festivals', אידיהן or עידיהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words sound almost the same but mean different things. With an א it means 'their calamity,' and with an ע it means 'their witnesses.' This is not an argument about the law. It is about which name the משנה uses for gentile festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings sound the same out loud. The argument is only about which letter the word starts with, א or ע, and what that spelling means.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav and Shmuel:
one teaches "eideihen" (with an alef)
and one teaches "eideihen" (with an ayin).

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of the משנה's word for 'their festivals': אידיהן (with an א) and עידיהן (with an ע).

steps.title: Neither reading is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that both readings are legitimate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it with an א is not mistaken, and the one who teaches it with an ע is not mistaken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that neither רב nor שמואל made a mistake. This sets up the next step, where each reading gets its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before explaining anything, the גמרא tells us that both readings are valid. It does not pick a winner, so the rest of the sugya will explain where each reading comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches (reads it this way)

phrases.english: The one who teaches "eideihen" (with an alef) is not mistaken
and the one who teaches "eideihen" (with an ayin) is not mistaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the two readings from step 4 and finds both acceptable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the א reading and the ע reading are legitimate.

steps.title: A verse supports each reading
steps.stepSummary: The א reading is based on 'כי קרוב יום אידם' (calamity), and the ע reading is based on 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו' (witnesses).
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it with an א is not mistaken, as it is written: 'For the day of their calamity is near.' The one who teaches it with an ע is not mistaken, as it is written: 'Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the 'not mistaken' line for each side, this time with a פסוק that backs up each reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אידם with an א in the פסוק means calamity, so calling the festivals 'calamities' points to the punishment they will bring. The word עדיהם with an ע means witnesses, so calling the festivals 'witnesses' shows that they testify to the idol worship of the גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: The one who teaches "eideihen" (with an alef) is not mistaken
as it is written: "For the day of their calamity is near"
and the one who teaches "eideihen" (with an ayin) is not mistaken
as it is written: "Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the line from step 5 and adds a פסוק for each reading.
steps.raayaObject: That each reading of the משנה's word is legitimate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 32:35 for the א reading, and ישעיהו 43:9 for the ע reading.

steps.title: Why doesn't the א reader use the ע reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the one who reads with an א did not choose the ע reading, since both are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who teaches it with an א, what is the reason he does not teach it with an ע?
steps.whatsHappening: Since both readings are fine, the גמרא asks why the א reader still prefers his own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once both readings are shown to have a source, the real question is which one is better. The גמרא asks each side to explain its preference, starting with the א side.

phrases.english: And the one who teaches "eideihen" (with an alef)
what is the reason he does not teach "eideihen" (with an ayin)?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the א reader prefers his reading over the equally valid ע reading.

steps.title: Calamity is the better word
steps.stepSummary: The א reader says the word for calamity is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: Calamity is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the א reader's answer: 'calamity' is the better way to describe these festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the most important thing is the final result, the downfall that will come upon the idol worshippers. So he names the festivals by that result.

phrases.english: He would say to you: calamity is preferable.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The calamity (the downfall itself) is the more fitting description.

steps.title: Why doesn't the ע reader use the א reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question of the other side: why did the ע reader not choose the א reading?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who teaches it with an ע, what is the reason he does not teach it with an א?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the ע reader and asks why he prefers 'witnesses' over 'calamity.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as step 7, aimed at the other side. It sets up a direct reply to the 'calamity is better' argument.

phrases.english: And the one who teaches "eideihen" (with an ayin)
what is the reason he does not teach "eideihen" (with an alef)?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּתָנֵי ״עֵידֵיהֶן״, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי ״אֵידֵיהֶן״
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ע reader prefers 'witnesses' over 'calamity.'

steps.title: Testimony is better, because it causes the calamity
steps.stepSummary: The ע reader says the testimony is what causes the calamity, so testimony is the more basic description.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: What causes them the calamity? The testimony they gave against themselves. Therefore, testimony is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ע reader answers that the calamity only comes because of the testimony, so 'witnesses' is the better word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He goes one step back from the result to its cause. The festivals testify to the idol worship of the גוים, and that testimony is what brings their downfall. So he names the festivals by the cause rather than the result.
steps.whatToRemember: Both readings are valid. The א reader names the festivals by their result (calamity), and the ע reader names them by its cause (the testimony of their own idol worship).

phrases.english: He would say to you:
What causes them the calamity?
the testimony that they testified about themselves
phrases.notes: By keeping their festivals, the גוים themselves show that they worship idols.

phrases.english: therefore testimony is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 and replies directly to the 'calamity is better' answer of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Testimony is the root cause of the calamity, so it is the more fitting description.

steps.title: The witnesses verse is about Israel, not the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source for the ע reading. The פסוק 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו' speaks about ישראל, as רבי יהושע בן לוי explains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this verse, 'Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified,' really written about the nations of the world? It is written about Israel! As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: all the מצוות Israel does in this world come and testify for them in the World to Come. 'Let them bring their witnesses and be justified' refers to Israel. 'Let them hear and say: it is true' refers to the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof brought earlier for the ע reading. It argues that the פסוק used there is not talking about אומות העולם at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the ע reading was based on 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו', read as witnesses against the nations. But רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the same words as Israel's מצוות testifying in their favor in עולם הבא. In his reading, the nations only appear in the second half of the פסוק, where they admit the truth. So this פסוק cannot support a word for testimony about the nations' downfall.

phrases.english: And this verse, 'Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified,'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק used back in step 6 as the source for the ע reading. ישעיהו 43:9

phrases.english: is it written about the nations of the world?
But it is written about Israel!
As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: All the מצוות that Israel does in this world
come and testify for them in the World to Come,
as it says: 'Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified'
these are Israel,
'Let them hear and say: It is true'
these are the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: והאי יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו באומות העולם כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source text that the ע reading relied on in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו' as the source for the ע reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that this פסוק refers to ישראל's מצוות testifying for them, not to witnesses against the nations, so it cannot be the source.

steps.title: A new verse: idols are witnesses against their makers
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different source for the ע reading, a פסוק calling idols 'their witnesses'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: the one who reads 'עידיהן' learns it from here: 'Those who make an idol are all emptiness, and their treasured things will not help, and they are their own witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by replacing the old source with a better one. This new פסוק clearly talks about idol worshippers and their witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the first source is dropped. The new פסוק from ישעיהו is about people who make idols and says the idols themselves are 'their witnesses'. So the ע reading still stands, but now it rests on a פסוק that really is about idolaters.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this signals that the earlier approach is dropped
Their treasured things, meaning their idols

steps.whatToRemember: The ע reading (עידיהן) is kept. Its source is now ישעיהו 44:9, where the idols are the witnesses against those who serve them.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
The one who reads 'eideihen' learns it from here:
'Those who make an idol are all emptiness'
and their treasured things will not help
and they are their own witnesses.'
phrases.notes: The idols themselves end up testifying against the people who made them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by giving a new source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the rejected source with a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ע reading came from 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו'
steps.terutzMaskana: The ע reading comes from 'ועדיהם המה' (ישעיהו 44:9), which is about idol makers

steps.title: In the future, ה׳ calls Torah learners to take their reward
steps.stepSummary: A new aggadah begins. In the future, הקב״ה will place a ספר תורה in His lap and invite whoever studied it to come for a reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא taught, and some say it was רבי שמלאי: in the future, הקב״ה will bring a ספר תורה, place it in His lap, and say: whoever occupied himself with it, let him come and take his reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the debate about spelling to a long aggadah. This line sets the scene for the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This aggadah explains ישעיהו 43:9, the same פסוק whose words 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו' were discussed in steps 6 and 11. The next step quotes its opening words, 'כל הגוים נקבצו יחדו'. The opening scene is an invitation to anyone who studied Torah, and the rest of the story shows how the nations try to claim that reward.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught or expounded, often a teaching drawn from פסוקים

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa taught,
and some say it was Rabbi Simlai:

phrases.aramaic: לְעָתִיד לָבֹא מֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring a Torah scroll
and place it in His lap, and say:
Whoever occupied himself with it,
let him come and take his reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic section after the spelling debate ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, הקב״ה will invite all who studied Torah to come and receive their reward.

steps.title: The nations rush in mixed together and are told to enter one by one
steps.stepSummary: The nations gather and come all mixed up. הקב״ה tells them to enter one nation at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, the nations of the world gather and come all mixed together, as it says, 'All the nations are gathered together.' הקב״ה says to them: do not come before Me all mixed up; rather, let each and every nation come in...
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the nations hurry in as one crowd to claim the reward. ה׳ orders them to come in separately, which sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נקבצו יחדו' ('gathered together') are read as the nations crowding in mixed together. הקב״ה's order to enter one nation at a time prepares for each nation being questioned on its own. The sentence continues into the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: All mixed together, in a jumble

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד מִתְקַבְּצִין וּבָאִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּעִרְבּוּבְיָא,
phrases.english: Immediately, the nations of the world gather and come all mixed together,
as it says: 'All the nations are gathered together, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 43:9. This is the same פסוק that contains 'יתנו עדיהם ויצדקו'.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says to them:
Do not come in before Me all mixed together;
rather, let each and every nation come in

steps.triggerLanguage: מיד מתקבצין ובאין אומות העולם בערבוביא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadah begun in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nations rush in together to claim the reward, and הקב״ה commands each nation to enter separately.
